problem: Given that the tangent line approximation to the function $f(x)$ at $x=\sqrt{2}$ overestimates the values of the function in the neighborhood of $x=\sqrt{2},$ which of the following must be true?

choices.value: $f(x)$ is concave down in the neighborhood of $x=\sqrt{2}$
$f(x)$ is concave up in the neighborhood of $x=\sqrt{2}$

feedback.problem: The graph of the function $y=f(x)$ passes through $(-3,-4)$ and is concave down on the interval $(-4,-2).$ If ${f}^{′}(-3)=3,$ estimate the value of $f(-2.9)$ using the tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at $x=-3$ and determine whether the approximation is an underestimate or overestimate.
feedback.worked_solution:
The tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at the point $a=-3$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a) \\  & =f(-3)+{f}^{′}(-3)(x+3).\end{aligned}
$$

The graph of the function passes through the point $(-3,-4),$ so we have $f(-3)=-4.$ Also, we're told that ${f}^{′}(-3)=3,$ so we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =-4+3(x+3) \\  & =-4+3x+9 \\  & =3x+5.\end{aligned}
$$

We can approximate $f(-2.9)$ by evaluating the tangent line approximation at $x=-2.9.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-2.9) & ≈L(-2.9) \\  & =3(-2.9)+5 \\  & =-8.7+5 \\  & =-3.7.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the function is concave down on the interval $(-4,-2),$ the linear approximation $L(x)$ is above the graph near $x=-3,$ and therefore we have an overestimate.
